title: Metro 2039 is a game about war that actually has something to say
text:
Earlier this year, publisher Deep Silver and developer 4A Studios published a blog post outlining its vision for Metro 2039. The studio revealed the game - being developed primarily in Ukraine amid the continued Russian invasion - is darker and focuses on the "cost of silence, the horrors of tyranny, and the price of freedom". How could it not be? The developers turn up to work every day not knowing if the power will go out, if they will have to take cover from a drone strike, if they will be able to see their loved ones that evening, or eat hot food when they get home. This is a game being developed in the middle of a warzone, and you better believe the final product is going to reflect that.

title: Gears of War: E-Day somehow feels exactly like a direct continuation of the original Xbox 360 trilogy, for better and for worse
text:
Marcus Fenix says something gruffly, his squad laughs, then a horde of Locust enemies rushes the team. The hulking figure of Marcus roadie-runs towards the nearest hip-high bit of cover, slams his muscly shoulder into the concrete, and starts laying down suppressing fire with his Lancer machine gun. Enemy bodies fall apart in meaty chunks, blood spatters on the stone floor. A grey-skinned drone breaks through the defensive line and levels his Gnasher at you, finger on the trigger. title: Synths, impossible physics, and an "erotic experience with a PS5 controller" - the side projects of game devs are a reminder creativity is undimmable
text:
If there's been one theme I'd pick out from the many of these past few years of gaming discontent, it's the sense of all-out assault on creativity. This is the thing that makes games what they are, that makes them successful, that earns people money and gives people a reason to do the job in the first place, but it's also the thing that seems to be valued least at so many of those making the decisions. To those people creativity is something to be funneled, moulded, directed or strictly defined. Often, I suspect, it's just not really something directly thought about at all. At best it's a nice buzzword to roll out as needed, but rare one that's even remotely understood.

title: What's your video game happy place?
text:
We all have our happy places: somewhere - real or otherwise - to escape, relax, and replenish away from the stresses of the modern world. Perhaps yours is in nature, lost in the reverie of a spirited hike up a windy hill, or sweatily squatting your cares away amid the pounding Daruda Sandstorms of your local gym. Perhaps your demands are simpler: the call of a good book and an escape into the realm of imagination, or the familiar celluloid embrace of a favourite film, or - as I finally drag this intro into relevance - the soothing rhythms of a beloved video game. Organisations such as the Game Music Festival have had such success with them they're doing multiple performances for multiple game franchises each year, selling out locations like the prestigious Royal Festival Hall on London's South Bank - sometimes in hours. That's where I watched a packed auditorium literally scream in excitement as Baldur's Gate 3 composer Borislav Slavov joined actor Andrew Wincott and singer Mariya Anastasova to perform Raphael's Final Act as an encore. title: The Biggest Gaming Stories That Happened Since GTA 5 Came Out 13 Years Ago
text:
The long, long wait for GTA 6 is coming to an end, as the game's November 19 release date approaches. Yes, there have been many leaks, but the genuine article arrives soon. 

It's been 13 years since GTA 5 launched in September 2013, and a lot has happened in the world of video games since then. When GTA 5 came out, Fortnite was not a thing. The live-service boom (and subsequent crash) hadn't happened yet. E3 was still a thriving, can't-miss annual summer event. Nintendo had just launched the ill-fated Wii U. 

In this post, we're running through some of the most notable gaming events and stories since GTA 5 launched more than a decade ago. To be sure, this is not an exhaustive list, and it does not touch on the many real-world, non-gaming high-profile events that have transpired. This list is all about big gaming stories, of which there have been many. 

A Comical Number Of Skyrim Ports

The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim released all the way back in 2011 for PS3, Xbox 360, and PC--nearly two years before GTA 5 launched. Since then, we haven't gotten a new mainline The Elder Scrolls game either, but we have gotten a ridiculous number of Skyrim ports across a bunch of different systems. Those include Skyrim for Nintendo Switch 1 and 2, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and various VR platforms. There's even, sort of, a port of Skyrim available for Amazon Alexa-enabled devices. Dubbed Skyrim Very Special Edition, it lets you explore Skyrim like it's an old-school text-adventure, so you can even keep playing as the Dragonborn while you make dinner. -- Gabe Gurwin

Three Watch Dogs Games

Shortly after the launch of GTA 5, Ubisoft released the original Watch Dogs, an open-world action game that offered similar freedom to Grand Theft Auto but with a particular focus on hacking infrastructure and weaponizing Chicago's electrical grid. It was followed by a far superior sequel set in San Francisco, Watch Dogs 2, a few years later, and the London-set Watch Dogs Legion in 2020. While the games--particularly Watch Dogs 2--certainly scratched a GTA-like itch, it's been radio silence on the series for several years. We're crossing our fingers for a true sequel to Watch Dogs 2 at some point. -- Gabe Gurwin

Halo Is On PlayStation

It would have been almost impossible to believe back in 2013, but a whole lot has changed over the last 13 years: Halo is now on PlayStation. During the Xbox 360 era, Microsoft was still sticking to a traditional exclusives-focused release strategy, with multiple Halo games releasing solely on Xbox 360. Even the real-time-strategy game Halo Wars initially released solely on Xbox 360, not coming to PC until 2016. But times have changed, and Microsoft opted to simultaneously launch Halo: Campaign Evolved on Xbox Series X|S, PC, and, yes, PlayStation 5. It remains to be seen if this will continue for future Halo games, as new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma seems interested in returning to exclusives, but it sure is weird to see a Halo game on Sony's system. -- Gabe Gurwin

GTA 5 Came To All These Other Platforms

Grand Theft Auto 5 was initially only available on Xbox 360 and PS3, with Rockstar following in its predecessors' footsteps by not launching day-and-date with PC. But the game did eventually come to PC, mod support and all, in 2015, and also released on Xbox One and PS4. But the wait for the next GTA has gone on so long that it also released for Xbox Series X|S and PS5, along with the separate GTA Online component. Up to this point, it hasn't come to Nintendo Switch or Switch 2, but it wouldn't be particularly shocking for that to happen in the future, as Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy is available on Switch. -- Gabe Gurwin

15+ Call of Duty Games 

The Call of Duty series is annualized, and there have been a lot of Call of Duty games released since GTA 5 came out in September 2013. In the time since Rockstar released GTA 5, Activision has released 13 mainline Call of Duty games, with a 14th, Modern Warfare 4, arriving in late October. In addition to all of those games, Activision launched the mobile game Call of Duty: Mobile in 2019, the battle royale game Call of Duty: Warzone in 2020, and then another mobile game, Call of Duty: Warzone Mobile, in 2024 (that game shut down in 2026). Also during the time since GTA 5 came out, the Call of Duty franchise changed hands, with Microsoft taking ownership of the franchise through its purchase of Activision Blizzard. -- Eddie Makuch

EA Gets A New CEO

GTA 5 and EA executive Andrew Wilson are connected by way of GTA 5 releasing and Wilson being promoted to CEO in the same month. Shortly after GTA 5 launched on September 17, 2013, Wilson was named CEO, replacing John Riccitiello on September 20. Both GTA 5 and Wilson did well for themselves in the decade-plus that followed, with GTA 5 selling exceptionally well and Wilson presiding over a run from about $25/share to $200+, increasing EA's market cap by billions upon billions. This culminated in Wilson and his team agreeing to sell the company to a group of investors led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in August 2026 for $55 billion. -- Eddie Makuch

The Death Of E3 

Not long after E3 2013 wrapped up in June that year, The Figueroa Hotel, located near the Los Angeles Convention Center where E3 was hosted, was adorned by impressive and gargantuan GTA 5 artwork. While GTA 5 and GTA Online would persist and thrive in the decade-plus that followed, E3 would not. Once a private trade show for industry professionals and media, E3 opened to the public in 2017, but it wouldn't last. After COVID led to the cancellation of the 2020 show, organizers held a virtual show in 2021. The 2022 event was canceled entirely, and though organizers promised a "reinvigorated showcase" for 2023, that didn't happen either--E3 was canceled permanently. Rockstar was known to make announcements at E3, as the company unveiled a brand-new PS3-exclusive spy game called Agent at E3 2009. -- Eddie Makuch

COVID And Its Impact On Gaming

The COVID-19 pandemic, which took hold in early 2020, had a massive impact on the world, of course, including the video game industry. Due to stay-at-home orders and general social distancing policies, people spent more time--and money--on things they could do at home. Naturally, home gym and fitness equipment sales soared, but so did spending on entertainment like video games. 

Sales of games and consoles skyrocketed, Twitch set unprecedented viewership records, and naturally, the surging spending on games made dollar-signs appear in executive and investor's eyes. Coupled with historically low costs to borrow money, this led to a situation where companies ramped up hiring and investors funded new studios, thinking the momentum might be sustainable. Painfully, it was not. Experts are now looking back and saying executives and investors mistook a bubble for a baseline. Subsequently, the past few post-COVID years have been some of the most tumultuous in recent times, with thousands of layoffs, numerous studio closures, countless game cancellations, and investment funding slowing down significantly. The pandemic may be behind us, but its impacts are still being felt today. -- Eddie Makuch

Destiny came and went

GTA 5 has been a hell of a success story for Rockstar Games, earning the studio critical acclaim. But GTA Online? That online portion of the game hit the mark for critical and commercial success, emerging as a giant in the live-service game space. Few games can compare to it, but for a brief time, Bungie's Destiny presented some stiff competition in a market where player attention spans are everything. It might have gotten off to a slow start, but a year later, Destiny was firing on all cylinders with the release of its Taken King expansion.

That momentum would begin to stall over the next few years, but once Bungie found its groove with Destiny 2's seasonal model, every Tuesday was a reason to sit down and enjoy everything that the weekly reset had to offer. For a few years, things were good: new content rolled out at a steady clip, new game modes made the wait for the next expansion flow by fast, and that gratifying grind for new loot was always welcome. That magic couldn't last forever, and following the release of The Final Shape in 2024, Destiny's days were numbered. The Edge of Fate saga saw two more compact expansions released, but by mid-2026, Bungie was ready to move on to new projects and its extraction-shooter Marathon--with mass layoffs being an unfortunate side effect.

Destiny's lifespan was short in the grand scheme of things, but ask anyone who played, those few years of gallivanting across planets and saving existence from would-be gods was downright magical. – Darryn Bonthuys

Saints Row fizzled out

Has there ever been a true GTA-killer? At one point, Saints Row was being positioned as the Bovril to GTA's Marmite, and it's not hard to see why. GTA adopted a more serious tone and became increasingly grounded in reality, whereas Saints Row operated like a Looney Tunes sandbox that embraced absurdity. Saints Row 2 got the ball rolling on that idea, but by the time that Saints Row 4 hit the scene, the shark had been jumped, flipped off, and killed with a rocket launcher. 

Volition's Saints Row reboot in 2022 was seen as an attempt to bring the franchise back to reality, but that's probably why it didn't take off with fans. With one foot planted in the realm of realism and another testing the waters of silliness, Saints Row ultimately felt like a game that didn't know what it wanted to be. The launch was middling, the game was buggy as hell during its first few weeks, and the whole experience felt like an open-world game designed by a committee, devoid of any real identity. Not long after, Volition Studios was shut down, and for now, it looks like the Saints Row franchise is dead. – Darryn Bonthuys

The Entire Phil Spencer Era Of Xbox

After joining Microsoft as an intern back in 1988, Phil Spencer was promoted to head of Xbox in 2014, kicking off his 12-year stint as one of the most notable figures in video games. In a situation eerily similar to current Xbox head, Asha Sharma, Spencer came in during an extremely volatile time for Xbox. Following the disastrous reveal of the Xbox One, Spencer was brought in to revitalize the brand and restore player trust, and did so by prioritizing backwards compatibility, fostering relationships with third-party studios, and creating Xbox Game Pass. 

Spencer was quickly embraced by the Xbox community, who championed him as a true gamer who understood what players wanted. But while his various initiatives and spending sprees might have endeared him to fans initially, his reputation soured over time due to his mismanagement of the various studios Xbox acquired and the rapidly increasing prices of both Game Pass and Xbox hardware. Spencer officially retired as Microsoft Gaming CEO earlier this year, leaving behind an extremely unstable company and a legacy tainted by layoffs, price hikes, and an overall weakening of the Xbox brand. And somehow, all of this happened in the span of time between GTA 5 and GTA 6. -- Jessica Cogswell

The Nintendo Switch's Entire Existence

A year before Grand Theft Auto 5 hit shelves, Nintendo unveiled a new (oddly named) console: the Wii U. Despite the success of its predecessor, the Wii, the Wii U was met with confusion and mixed reactions, both of which led to it becoming Nintendo's lowest-selling home console of all time (if we aren't counting the Virtual Boy). Following this commercial failure, Nintendo quickly went back to the drawing board. Five years later, Nintendo released its next console: the Nintendo Switch.

In combining its talent for creating fantastic handheld systems and the public's desire for a home console with a little something for everyone, Nintendo struck gold. The Switch is now the second-best-selling console of all time, with nearly 156.6 million units sold--less than 4 million units shy of the PlayStation 2. In 2025, Nintendo released the successor to the console, the Nintendo Switch 2, which has already hit nearly 23.7 million units sold--a whopping 10 million more units than the Wii U sold across its five-year life span.

In addition to these consoles being tremendously successful themselves, they've also helped usher in a new golden era for Nintendo games. Titles like The Legend of the Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Fire Emblem: Three Houses, Donkey Kong: Bananza, and Super Mario Odyssey have effectively reshaped their respective series; less active franchises, like Metroid, Luigi's Mansion, Pokemon Snap, Kirby, and Animal Crossing, have been reinvigorated with critically acclaimed new entries; and the release of definitive versions of Super Smash Bros. and Mario Kart have made the Switch the ultimate destination for all things Nintendo. Combine all this with the addition of Nintendo Online's catalog of games, and it truly feels as though the Switch is Nintendo's pièce de résistance. -- Jessica Cogswell

Consoles Got A Lot More Expensive

Although video games have technically never been cheaper, console prices have risen astronomically in the time since GTA 5's release. These price hikes have been especially bad in recent years, as tariffs and the ongoing components crisis--linked largely to the rise of AI data centers--have made the cost of making consoles a lot more expensive. As a result, consumers are now paying more for five-year-old consoles than they would have if they purchased them day one.

The Xbox Series X, originally sold for $500 when it launched in November 2020, now rests at $800--and it's already rumored that the console will see a price hike again in 2027. The PlayStation 5 Digital Edition has risen from $400 to $600, while the version with a disc drive has jumped from $500 to $650. Even Nintendo has increased its console prices, with both the Switch 2 and Switch OLED seeing $50 price increases. And don't even get me started on how unreasonable it would be to build a PC these days. -- Jessica Cogswell

title: Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026: All The Biggest Announcements, Games, And Trailers
text:
Gamescom Opening Night Live is here, and once again, it was a bumper night full of new game reveals, gameplay deep-dives, and more from Geoff Keighley's second big show of the year.

There were new trailers for plenty of big games, like Gears of War: E-Day, Metro 2039, and Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. We also got a whole bunch of new reveals, and in case you missed it, you can catch up below.

Worms: Galactic Tactics

Our first trailer of the preshow was for a new Worms tactics game that takes a page from the XCOM playbook. It looks like the original Worms is also coming back in some form.

Train Sim World 7

The next chapter in the long-running Train Sim World series launches on September 15.

RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks

Think you have what it takes to run the ultimate theme park? You can put your skills to the test when RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks launches in early access soon.

RollerCoaster Tycoon Is Back, And This Time It Has Bubsy

Aniimo

An action-RPG rooted in ancient Chinese creation mythology, players will take on titanic monsters as the Spirit Pearl, the first being forged by the Goddess of Creation Nüwa.

Need some horror that's all about things that go bump in the night? Perceptum looks like it'll scratch that itch when it launches in 2027.

Acornia: Mirror Worlds

This bake-and-brawl management adventure game from Splashteam continues to look adorable, and it's out next year.

Valor Mortis

Here's one more trailer for the upcoming first-person souls-like Valor Mortis from Ghostrunner Studio One More Level, which launches on October 13 for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.

TankRat

We've got a release date for TankRat, where you'll battle swarms of corrupted mech-monsters from your heavily armed vehicle. It's out on January 17, 2027.

Humankind 2

The sequel to 2021's Humankind aims to improve on the 4X strategy formula, and once again, players can guide their nation through various eras of human history. It'll be coming to PC in 2027.

Humankind 2 Forces You To Deal With The Consequences Of Climate Change

Murals

What do centuries-old fables like The Little Mermaid, Rapunzel, and Hansel & Gretel all have in common? Besides the original fiction being nightmare fuel, they're also all featured in Murals, an original IP from Disney Illusion Island developer Dlala Studios. The isometric action-adventure game is set across multiple famous fairy tales, and players will control a nameless hero who must brave dark, twisted takes on these beloved stories.

Murals Turns Famous Fairy Tales Into A Silly Action-Adventure

Age Twisters

Age Twisters is a two-player co-op narrative adventure game, where you'll play as a grandfather and granddaughter who team up to solve puzzles. It looks adorable, but it has no release date yet.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword

In case you missed it, there's a demo out there for Onimusha: Way of the Sword. And if you've already played it? Then it's time to boot it up again, as Capcom has added more content to this early--and free--slice of the game.

Mariachi Legends

I didn't have a Mexican vampire metroidvania on my Gamescom bingo card, but Mariachi Legends is scratching an itch for that very specific scratch I didn't know I had. It launches in April 2027.

Elta: Defy All Gods

Get ready to brawl your way out of corrupted worlds in Elta: Defy All Gods. You've also got an adorable dragon-god companion, free-form melee combat, and fluid platforming, so this might be worth keeping an eye on.

Nodusfall

HoYoverse made a name for itself with anime-inspired live-service games, but for its next title? It looks like the developer is taking on Elden Ring developer From Software with a high fantasy adventure that looks gorgeous. Called Nodusfall, players take on the role of a Weaver in this co-op action game.

Genshin Impact Maker’s Nodusfall Sure Looks Like Multiplayer Elden Ring

Rainbow Six Tactics

It's the first brand-new Rainbow Six game in many years! Rainbow Six Tactics features 15 unique Operators, and players will take part in missions across the globe in this XCOM-inspired title. It's out in 2027.

Rainbow 6 Tactics Looks Like If Siege And XCOM: Chimera Squad Had A Baby

Gears of War: E-Day

After a fun weekend in the Gears of War: E-Day multiplayer beta, the focus is on the story with this new trailer for the game. It's the darkest hour for humanity as Emergence Day leaves cities across Sera ruined, but it looks like humanity isn't ready to go down without a fight. Gears of War: E-Day launches on October 6.

Gears Of War: E-Day Seems To Miss The Point Of Prequels

Ananta

NetEase's free-to-play GTA-meets-Spider-Man game Ananta is all about keeping the peace and building a social media empire. It looks wonderfully ridiculous, and it launches on January 15, 2027 for PC and PS5.

Ananta’s New Trailer Goes Hard On Memes

Silent Hill Townfall

In case the next few months don't look busy enough, you can try out some small-town Scottish horror in Silent Hill Townfall. The new trailer showed off more of the spooky game in action, and it's the first Silent Hill to be played from a first-person perspective. It's out on September 24.

Resonance: A Plague Tale

The next Plague Tale game is also out soon, and instead of having too many rats, it focuses on puzzles, exploration, and combat. You can check out the launch trailer for it above.

Sea of Remnants

We next got a fresh look at Sea of Remnants, a pirate-themed RPG with some stylish visuals. I can't say I'm too big a fan of the trailer's use of cheesy country music, though.

Tides of Annihilation

Your ears are not deceiving you! That is indeed Resident Evil Requiem's Grace Ashcroft actor, Angela Sant'Albano, taking over the role of Gwendolyn in Tides of Annihilation. The Arthurian Legend action game continues to look great, and you can wishlist it on Steam now.

Lofsong

Explore, listen, and unravel a hidden language buried in stone and sound: Lofsong. We still don't know much about this exploration-heavy puzzle adventure, but it has incredibly striking visuals.

Mega Man: Dual Override

It wouldn't be a Mega Man game without a few boss fights! We got our first look at one of the new bosses you'll fight, Twinkle Girl, and it looks like Proto Man is also ready to get in Mega Man's way.

Wait, Is Mega Man: Dual Override Just Mega Man X Now?

Rayman Legends Retold

Rayman speedrunning his way through a food-themed level while pasta-monsters attempt to eat him and a remix of the Macarena plays? It's good to have the limbless hero back. You can experience this for yourself when the game launches on October 1.

PUBG Ded.Net

The new PUBG game, Ded.Net, looks kind of bonkers, and I dig it. Very wild, many bullets, and it looks like Michael Bay's take on Twin Peaks.

New PUBG Game Ded Net Looks Nothing Like PUBG

Control Resonant

It's our second game with a resonance-themed title, Control Resonant! The Control sequel looks like an action-packed blast of fun, and it launches in September for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.

Once Human

You can grab this game for free on PC and console, starting today.

Game of Thrones: War for Westeros

A proper look at the gameplay for Game of Thrones: War for Westeros confirms that maybe I'll need to use some proper tactics to take down the Night King, instead of throwing soldiers at him until he runs out of arrows and sharp swords. It comes to PC in early 2027.

Game Of Thrones: War For Westeros Will Let The White Walkers Win

Dust: Origins

An isometric shooter from the makers of Darksiders: Genesis, developer Airship Syndicate, where you have to mow down monsters? Sign me up.

The Blood Of Dawnwalker

Another game out soon, The Blood of Dawnwalker got a new story trailer ahead of its release in early September.

Crimson Desert: Enhanced Edition

It's Crimson Desert, but enhanced! This updated version of the game is out now.

Exodus

The new trailer for Exodus showed off more of the spiritual successor to Mass Effect. Full of dialogue choices, cover to hunker behind during firefights, and exotic powers to wield, the biggest surprise was that you can recruit a super-intelligent octopus to your team and put them inside a mechanized warsuit. The game launches on April 7, 2027.

Exodus, The New Sci-Fi RPG From Former BioWare Devs, Finally Gets A Launch Date

Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons

Following that sci-fi trailer, it was time for some fantasy with the first look at the gameplay for Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons. In this original single-player action-adventure, you'll play as Kaatri, a warrior who makes a fateful pact to wield dark magic against even darker powers. The game also features Maggie Robertson as Tasha, who's kind of a big deal in Dungeons & Dragons.

Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons Doesn’t Seem Too Concerned With The “D&D” Part Of Its Title

1,001 Threads of Mizan

Inspired by the ancient tales of Arabian folklore, 1,001 Threads of Mizan looks like another fun fantasy game where you'll take on all manner of strange monsters. And some of them are the size of mountains, but at least you have a magic carpet that you can ride to even the odds!

1001 Threads Of Mizan Could Be The Arabian Nights Game You’ve Been Waiting For

Silver Palace

It's another anime-inspired live-service game trailer, but admittedly, the music for this new look at Silver Palace slaps, and the visuals also look pretty wild.

Metro 2039

Described as a game about consequence, Metro 2039's new trailer showed off an impressively bleak post-apocalyptic world. With the Nova Reich now ruling Moscow with an iron fist, it's up to the Stranger to take down Hunter, a familiar--and heroic--face from the first Metro games. The game also has a release window of February 2027.

Metro 2039 Explores The Horror Humans Can Commit In Latest Gameplay Trailer

Hitman: World of Assassination

The Doggfather, Snoop Dogg, is coming to Hitman: World of Assassination, and I'm not making this up. He'll be a free Elusive Target for Hitman players starting August 27.

Aion 2

Time for something a little less ridiculous, as we got a new look at the MMO Aion. A new teaser that showed a lot of skin.

Afterworld: Your Empire From the Ashes

Paradox Interactive showed off Afterworld next, which appears to be a post-apocalyptic city-builder. That's a fresh spin on the genre, and it looks perfect for Mad Max fans thirsty for a chance to rebuild society.

Petit Planet

Does HoYoverse ever sleep? The Genshin Impact studio revealed a trailer for Petit Planet, a cozy life-sim game set in a galactic world.

Mewgenics

I'm absolutely jealous of everyone at the Koelnmesse who got to enjoy a live performance of a Mewgenics track. The game is also coming to consoles on September 8.

Alies: Fireteam Elite 2

It's in the Gamescom vents! Aliens: Fireteam 2 has just launched, and it once again pits the Colonial Marines against an army of perfect organisms--and one walking Facehugger monstrosity that gives me the shivers.

1666: Amsterdam

We're still thinking that 1666: Amsterdam needs a lot of work, but that's what early access is for. The new trailer showed off more of the supernatural game in action, as well as how you can use cat scratches to control the feeble-minded. You can try it out now via Steam Early Access.

Showa American Story

Showa American Story continues to be the weirdest thing around, and that's why we're keen to play this oddball action game. The new trailer showed off more gameplay and absurdity.

Road Kings

Have you ever wanted to drive an 18-wheeler across the US and pretend that you're taking part in a drama-free version of Smokey and the Bandit? Well, Road Kings looks like a 10-4 on that request, good buddy. You can start playing this March 11, 2027.

Stage Tour

Out later this year, Stage Tour is a new game in the same vein as Guitar Hero and Rock Band. It features over 90 licensed songs, plastic instruments, and, yes, this trailer used Motley Crue's "Kickstart My Heart."

The New Guitar Hero–Err, Stage Tour–Has 90+ Songs On Its Setlist And Gets A Release Date

Crazy Taxi

Yeah yeah yeah yeah! Crazy Taxi is making a comeback, and Sega dropped a new trailer for the game's multiplayer mode, which looks wild.

Turok Origins

Considering just how packed the rest of the year is with new game releases, Turok Origins announcing a delay to Spring 2027 makes perfect sense. The Destiny-inspired game features teams of superpowered players fighting some very nasty dinosaurs.

Gravhounds

Dogs with guns! It's a match made in heaven. Gravhounds looks like a mix of tower defense and third-person shooting, and it'll be out later this year.

Gravhounds Reveal Trailer Sends Good Boys Into A Sci-Fi Battle

Lego Skylines

A Lego city-building game, where everything just clicks into place? This Lego game is going to make a lot of money.

Lego Skylines Is A Genius Idea For A Cities: Skylines Spin-Off

Exterminauts

You can never have too many co-op shooters where you take down hordes of nasty alien bugs, and Exterminauts looks like it'll be a nice addition to my collection of Starship Troopers-inspired games. You can wishlist it on Steam now, but there's no release date yet.

Path of Exile 2

Action-RPG Path of Exile 2 releases in 1.0 on December 11.

Path Of Exile 2 Is Finally Getting Its Full Release, And It’ll Be Free To Play

Heroes of Might and Magic 3 remake

The critically acclaimed turn-based strategy game is making a comeback, and this remake will also include its two expansions. Rebuilt in full 3D and sporting 4K visuals, players can once again explore a vibrant fantasy world in this reimagined classic.

No Law

A brief look at No Law showed off a game that looks heavy on action, suspense, and cyberpunk themes. It's the work of a small Swedish developer, Neon Giant.

Cyberpunk 2077’s Sequel Is Years Away, But No Law Might Fill The Gap

Cinder City

Cinder City looks like a cinematic third-person shooter set in a near-future version of Seoul that has seen better days. There's no release date yet, but the new trailer showed off some imaginative visuals.

Ontos

Remember Ontos? It's a sci-fi mystery set on the repurposed moon hotel Samsara, and the first look at it was full of some very disturbing imagery. The new trailer didn't disappoint, as Soma developer Frictional Games' new title revealed a disturbing use for mice.

Pony Island 2: Panda Circus

Inscryption developer Daniel Mullins has a new game on the way, called Pony Island 2. It's described as "a phantasmagorical voyage through time, myth, divinity, and video games," where you'll attempt to escape gods and keep your sanity intact. Sadly, it has no ponies.

Zoopunk

And now for something completely different: talking animals wielding all kinds of weapons in a third-person action game.

The Defiant

A new first-person shooter that unfolds on the Chinese battlefields of World War II.

Like or Die

Billed as a team-based survival FPS where streamers clash in a fierce battle for survival, Like or Die is taking influencer culture to a new extreme. Players can also reshape the battlefield with blocks in the ultimate survival livestream.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation

The final chapter in the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy is out in Spring 2027, and the new trailer for it showed off an epic race to stop Sephiroth from destroying the planet. With the various Weapons of the planet rising up, it looks like Cloud and friends have their work cut out for them.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Gamescom Trailer Is All About The Weapons

The Witcher 3

Closing out the show was The Witcher 3, which is getting a new remastered edition on September 29. It'll be a free upgrade for owners of the game, and it includes various enhancements, such as upgraded graphics, improved combat, traversal, overhauled monsters, improved skill trees, and a photo mode. It also includes the two Witcher 3 expansions, Blood and Wine and Hearts of Stone, for free. We got a look at the upcoming third expansion, too.

The Witcher 3 Remastered Is Adding Dozens Of Upgrades And It Might Be Free For You

title: Gravhounds Reveal Trailer Sends Good Boys Into A Sci-Fi Battle
text:
Gamescom Opening Night Live is always full of surprises, and this year, indie developer Octopus Panic made a splash with a first look at its new action-builder game Gravhounds. As seen in the reveal trailer below, Gravhounds takes place in a future where interstellar exploration and colonization have become the domain of man's best friend.

Although the trailer states that the titular Gravhounds have been "bred" for this life, their humanoid appearance suggests more than a little genetic engineering was responsible for this turn of events. In fact, there's no sign of human life at all on this hostile alien world, but the Gravhounds themselves seem human enough.

The gameplay supports 1-4 players as they attempt to build up resources for a new colony while holding on to the potential promise of coming home. Upgrades appear to play a major role in the main characters' survival, especially when they get overwhelmed by alien forces that really don't want them around at all.

According to Gravhounds' Steam page, the game's early-access period will last at least six months. It will "include the core Gravhound experience," but we plan to expand its breadth, depth, and replayability on the road to 1.0," reads the statement. Both solo and co-op campaigns will be playable during this initial release.

Gravhounds' early-access release will hit Xbox Series X|S and PC on November 2. It will also be available on day one with Xbox Game Pass.

title: The Witcher 3 Remastered Is Adding Dozens Of Upgrades And It Might Be Free For You
text:
It may not be The Witcher 4, but the first real look at The Witcher 3's new DLC, Songs of the Past, might just make the wait a little easier, especially when it's coming soon after a free upgrade to The Witcher 3 Remastered, as was newly revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live.

Developer CD Projekt Red showed off the upcoming expansion (just don't call it DLC) as part of Gamescom Opening Night Live, revealing new details about the over-a-decade-later expansion coming to The Witcher 3.

But this came after the reveal of the game's remastered version, whose changes and additions were numerous, including improved controls, a skill tree revamp, expanded photo mode, both past expansions, and tons more. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered launches on September 29 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and it's free if you already own The Witcher 3.

All announced changes for The Witcher 3 Remastered

  • Upgraded visuals
  • Enhanced combat
  • Improved traversal and movement
  • Revamped mount handling
  • Improved monster behaviors
  • Revamped skill tree
  • Transmogrification
  • Expanded photo mode
  • New combat finishers
  • Cross-platform mods
  • Immersive meditation
  • Refined animations
  • New quest tracking
  • UI improvements
  • Looting rework
  • Refreshed motion blur
  • New accessibility features
  • Updated textures

Songs of the Past has been described as being similar in size and scope to The Witcher 3's previous two expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine. It's currently slated to release in 2027 but was orginally planned for 2026.

There are still plenty of questions about Songs of the Past, namely how it might connect to the events of The Witcher 4, which will star Ciri instead of Geralt. CD Projekt Red recently confirmed The Witcher 4 is targeting a 2028 release.

title: Cyberpunk 2077’s Sequel Is Years Away, But No Law Might Fill The Gap
text:
From the stage of Gamescom Opening Night Live, No Law brought out the cyberpunk flair during a stage show that was often dominated by anime games, dark fantasy souls-likes, and cozy offerings. There's nothing cozy in No Law, though fans of Cyberpunk 2077 will find aesthetics that seem familiar. 

While No Law looks a lot like Cyberpunk 2077 when all hell breaks loose, it should be noted that such is the main attraction of Neon Giant's follow-up to The Ascent, as No Law is said to be a first-person shooter, not an RPG. 

No Law is set for release in 2027 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X.

title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Gamescom Trailer Is All About The Weapons
text:
Following its official reveal at Summer Games Fest, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation made another appearance at Gamescom Opening Night Live, following a brief introduction from director Naoki Hamaguchi. This trailer was centered almost entirely on the Weapons, massive beasts that appear to have a larger role to play in this final part of the trilogy.

The cinematic trailer showed Rufus Shinra giving an address following recent world events, and the world has become overrun with Weapons. Those kaiju-like beasts were a part of the original Final Fantasy 7, including as optional bosses, but they seem to have a much bigger role in the story here. In dialogue the cast talks about them being guardians of the planet, and humans are seen as a harmful invasive species. The trailer showed off Ultima Weapon and Emerald Weapon in particular, but there may be more.

The trailer also showed off a good bit of the full cast, an aerial battle in Cid's Highwind, and ground battles against familiar Final Fantasy foes like Typhon (aka Mr. Chupon, for you old-school fans).

The final chapter in the Final Fantasy Remake trilogy--but maybe not the last game in this series--Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is building on the groundwork laid by its predecessors with new content and some fine-tuning of its open-world gameplay. One of the new features is the FITS system that allows you to equip Cloud and the gang with new roles in combat, and if you want to stick to the golden path without having to worry about stopping to take part in a game of cards, minigames will be more optional in the threequel.

For more on the game, you can also check out dozens of screenshots showing off the world of Midgar, why the planetary weapons were game director Naoki Hamaguchi's favorite thing to remake, and who's voicing Sephiroth this time.

title: Path Of Exile 2 Is Finally Getting Its Full Release, And It’ll Be Free-To-Play
text:
Path of Exile 2 debuted a new gameplay trailer during Gamescom Opening Night Live, which revealed that the action-role-playing sequel will finally launch out of early access on December 11.

The latest gameplay trailer offers a snippet of the sequel's narrative setup, as well as a look at its faster action compared to its predecessor. Like the first game, Path of Exile 2 will offer incredibly deep class customization through hundreds of active and passive skill gems, with a deep emphasis on endgame content that will be composed of over 100 maps and grueling boss fights.

Path of Exile 2 entered early access in December 2024 across PC, Xbox Series X|S, and PlayStation 5. Participating in early builds of the game wasn't free, but developer Grinding Gear Games has confirmed that the game will be going free-to-play when it does launch into 1.0 later this year.

If you're already playing Path of Exile 2 or want to get the most out of it when it does launch, you can sign up on the game's official mailing list and receive exclusive in-game rewards in the lead-up to release.

If December is too far away, Diablo IV's latest expansion launched earlier this year and continues to expand on Blizzard's role-playing epic in all the rights ways.

title: All Anyone At Gamescom Can Talk About Is Dolly Parton
text:
This year's Gamescom Opening Night Live ceremony just came to an end, and the livestreamed showcase had no shortage of highly anticipated announcements and trailers. From a closer look at the upcoming Witcher 3 DLC and the announcement of two PUBG spin-offs, to new glimpses of Control: Resonant, Silent Hill: Townfall, and Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, ONL seemed to have something for everyone. There was even a live performance of a track from the Mewgenics soundtrack.

But between demands for a new Path of Exile 2 trailer (which finally materialized 90 minutes into the showcase) and random declarations of "GTA 6!!!," one message kept popping up in the showcase's live Twitch chat: #RIPDOLLY.

Just moments into the live broadcast, country singer and pop culture icon Dolly Parton's death was announced via an Instagram post shared by her nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver.

Parton passed away at 80, after decades of smash country hits and admirable charitable giving. Aside from appearing in several casino games, Parton had very little to do with gaming, her biggest contributions being her 2020 collaboration with Word With Friends and the inclusion of her songs "9 to 5" and "Odd Jobs" in 2009's Pop'n Music for the Nintendo Wii. (Though she did appear in her own pinball machine in 1979.)

But despite her lack of deep connections to the world of gaming, homages to Parton continued to flood the chat even as Gamescom's opening showcase entered its second hour. And in his announcement of her death, Parton's nephew Bryan Seaver explained things perfectly.

"My family and I have shared a lifetime of beautiful memories with Dolly, but so have you," he said. "She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family whether you liked it or not. Our family and the team she has entrusted with her legacy will work diligently to ensure her spirit will live with us forever. Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy; he farmed the soil, [while] she farmed songs and happiness."

Perhaps that's the essence of it. Parton connected with everyone--not just country music lovers or fans of her many films. Like games themselves, Parton was a fond part of many of our childhoods. Her charisma was so strong that her memory managed to steal the show at a gaming showcase held half a world away from her home in Tennessee, where her family says she passed peacefully. 

Image credit: Getty Images / Ian Gavan

title: Lego Skylines Is A Genius Idea For A Cities: Skylines Spin-Off
text:
Paradox Interactive and Iceflake Studios validated some recent leaks at Gamescom Opening Night Live by announcing Lego Skylines. As its title suggests, it's a spin-off of the city builder Cities: Skylines where everything is made out of Lego.

A press release for Lego Skylines explains that the game will start on a single plot of land, allowing players to build and customize their house. From there, they can build up to an entire neighborhood and then a giant city. Like Cities: Skylines, you'll have to manage the distribution of electricity, food, and water, and build parks, museums, sports parks, and more to keep your citizens happy.

After the rocky launch of Cities: Skylines 2, Iceflake Studios took over the development of that game from Colossal Order. Iceflake is also the developer working on Lego Skylines, with director Lasse Liljedahl saying in a press release that "most of us at Iceflake grew up building Lego sets" and that he is excited to make a city builder that's a "more personal experience."

Generally, I find the high-level pitch for Lego Skylines to be a great game concept, and I'm definitely excited to see more. Lego tie-in games have been a pretty great run recently with Lego Voyagers, Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, and Lego Party. Hopefully, Lego Skylines is as good as it sounds and won't have the performance issues on PC that Cities: Skylines 2 had at release.

Lego Skylines does not have a release date, but it is confirmed for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2.

title: Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons Doesn’t Seem Too Concerned With The “D&D” Part Of Its Title
text:
After nearly a year of silence, Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons has reemerged to give sword and sorcery fans a first look at its third-person gameplay. Warlock's gameplay reveal came during Gamescom Opening Night Live, and featured a lengthy trailer showcasing how the game's spell-slinging combat will work.

Based on its latest trailer, Warlock forgoes sticking to the same formula many D&D-based adventure games tend to use, placing an emphasis on spells and combat rather than roleplay and replicating the tabletop experience. This might not appeal to those seeking a more traditional D&D-like experience--or those who are baffled by main character Katri's seemingly infinite spell slots--but its dark fantasy visuals, snappy spellcasting, and Witcher-esque gameplay certainly look fun.

In addition to a first look at gameplay, the trailer also gave us a bit more information regarding the game's setting. It seems as though Warlock will follow Katri's journey through Ravenloft's Domains of Dread. Darkon, the largest and most powerful of these domains, was seen in the trailer; we can only hope that a Darklord Azalin appearance will follow.

Warlock was announced during the 2025 The Game Awards via a stylish heavy metal trailer that spotlighted the game's main character, Katri. In an interview last year, developer Invoke Studios said players will always play as Katri, but may meet other characters and form alliances with them while adventuring.

Earlier this year, it was announced that Maggie Robertson--best known for her performances as Lady Dimitrescu in Resident Evil: Village and Orin the Red in Baldur's Gate 3--would be joining Warlock as Tasha, a Dungeons & Dragons icon whom fans are likely familiar with. Known also as Iggwilv, Zybilna, and The Witch Queen, Tasha is the creator of a Domain of Delight, Prismeer, and one of the universe's most powerful archfey. In Warlock, Tasha serves as Katri's patron, granting her immense power in exchange for obedience.

This isn't Invoke's first stab at a D&D adventure. The studio, formerly Tuque Studios, was also behind 2021's not exactly well-received D&D: Dark Alliance reboot.

Warlock is slated for a 2027 release.

title: The New Guitar Hero–Err, Stage Tour–Has 90+ Songs On Its Setlist And Gets A Release Date

title: Metro 2039 Explores The Horror Humans Can Commit In Latest Gameplay Trailer
text:
The Metro games have never shied away from shoving players into a bleak post-apocalyptic world, but in Metro 2039, things are looking especially grim. Ahead of its release in 2027, a new gameplay trailer for Metro 2039 was revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live, showing how players will have to deal with a new regime that has risen from the ashes of the nuclear war that turned the world into a radioactive wasteland.

The gameplay showcased several hallmarks of the Metro's distinct action. These include dangerous metro tunnels filled with soldiers, monsters inhabiting the radiation-filled surface, and the many, many guns you'll have to dispatch them with. Like previous entries, you'll be able to craft weapons to suit your playstyle, with the gameplay showcasing an aggressive approach to the series' stealth action.

While Metro 2039 still features mutated monsters and ghouls, it seems 4A Games is focusing more on the atrocities humans can commit in this sequel. As described by developers on stage at Opening Night Live, Metro 2039 is about consequences: the cost of silence, the horror of tyranny, the price of freedom. It is clear the studio is drawing from its experience of developing the sequel while enduring the ongoing war in Ukraine.

Metro 2039 features a new protagonist, known as the Stranger. A new power has risen in the form of the Spartan Order, which has evolved from a force for good in the older Metro games into a twisted, authoritarian movement known as the Novareich. Led by Hunter--the very same Spartan Ranger from Metro 2033--the Stranger comes out of exile and embarks on a journey through the remains of Moscow to take down the Novareich and Hunter, its Führer.

Developer 4A Games says that Metro 2039 will be a shocking entry in the series: one where players will have to master exploration, survival, combat, and stealth skills to stand a chance at seeing the Stranger's mission through to the end. Despite being a sequel to the original trilogy, 4A Games says this will be an ideal point to jump in if you haven't yet, too. Metro 2039 launches for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S in February 2027.

title: NBA 2K27 Teases GTA 6 Crossover Of Some Kind
text:
2K Sports has released a new trailer for NBA 2K27 today, and it features a reference to GTA 6 that is prompting people to theorize about what it may mean. The Season 1 trailer for NBA 2K27 does a lot more than just show off what's coming in Season 1--it also hints at Seasons 2 and 3.

As you can see in the trailer below, the imagery and styling for Season 3 is plainly referencing GTA 6 with its palm trees, font, and colors. Police sirens can be heard as well, which is another nod to GTA.

The video doesn't specifically state when NBA 2K27's Season 3 will begin. However, it does confirm that Season 2 starts October 16.

If seasons are as long as they have historically be in the past, that would mean Season 3 could start around the end of November. And that lines up nicely with GTA 6's release on November 19.

This isn't the first time that GTA 6 and basketball have been connected. One of the GTA 6 gameplay leaks showed main character Jason dribbling a basketball and shooting hoops at his house, with many taking this to mean basketball will be a minigame of sorts in GTA 6.

That seems like a safe bet, as does GTA 6 crossing over with NBA 2K27 in some capacity. Take-Two, which owns Rockstar and 2K, might see a rising tide lifting all ships, after all.

NBA 2K27 launches into early access on August 26 for people who preordered the game's premium editions. It unlocks for everyone on September 4.

title: Ananta’s New Trailer Goes Hard On Memes
text:
Today, during Gamescom Opening Night Live, NetEase showed off new gameplay for Ananta, its upcoming open-world anime action-adventure. The trailer featured multiple cityscapes, a January 15 release date, and ... internet memes?

Indeed, the gameplay was highlighted by multiple references to internet jokes and slang, including the Gatsby lifting glass meme, the Dragon Ball Z "Yamcha death" meme, and the main hero being called the "yeetmaster."

Outside of the jokes, the three-minute trailer showed both Nova City and Lingyun City, the two open areas that will make up Ananta's setting. We see traversal via flying car, motorbike, skateboard, and more as the "yeetmaster" meets multiple characters and get into some close calls while traveling through both cities.

Ananta will see players take the role of a single influncer with the goal of saving the world by "going viral." The influencer will meet over 100 characters throughout the quest, each with their own individual questlines, and some can be recruited as allies along the way.

For more on Gamescom, check out our coverage on Ubisoft's Rainbow Six Tactics, Hoyoverse's Nodusfall, and the return of Roller Coaster Tycoon.

title: Game Of Thrones: War For Westeros Will Let The White Walkers Win
text:
It's still going to be a while before Game of Thrones: War for Westeros arrives, but at Gamescom Opening Night Live, developer Playside showed off some gameplay to make the wait a little bit easier.

First announced in 2025--and originally scheduled for a 2026 launch--Game of Thrones: War for Westeros is a real-time strategy game that features several of the franchise's legendary Houses--Lannister, Stark, and Targaryen--as well as the sinister forces of the Night King. With each faction vying to take control of the Seven Kingdoms, it's up to players to command their armies and lead them to victory.

Hero units look to play a major role in War for Westeros' RTS gameplay, with characters like Tywin Lannister, Jon Snow, and others shown to have special abilities that can turn the tide of battle. And Daenerys Targaryen, of course, has a dragon, which seems like it will be more than a little overpowered.

The trailer gives a glimpse of this, and how players will be able to rewrite Game of Thrones history. At one point Robb Stark can be seen cutting down Jamie Lannister before later approaching the Iron Throne. Someone must have warned him about the Red Wedding. It also teases what the ending of Game of Thrones may have looked like had the White Walkers won, with the end of the trailer showing the Night King sitting on the throne triumphantly.

The final season of Game of Thrones back in 2019 is largely remembered now as one of the greatest fumbles in the history of television, so it will be interesting to see how War for Westeros will let players change events to their liking. Don't like the fact that Bran the Broken was seemingly chosen at random to sit the Iron Throne? Now you can choose who wins, and (hopefully) create a more satisfying ending than the one from the show.

Designed to be a nod to classic RTS games, War for Westeros features a single-player campaign and multiplayer modes for when you want to test your skills against real players across the world. After being out of the limelight for many years, real-time strategy games appear to be making a soft comeback, as Battle for Westeros follows in the wake of several other popular games in the genre, like Age of Empires 4, Age of Mythology: Retold, and Homeworld 3.

Upcoming titles like Stronghold 4 and Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 also suggest that there's still a healthy appetite for old-school strategy games. Currently, the Game of Thrones series is owned and controlled by Warner Bros. Discovery, but that could all change if Paramount succeeds in its $100 billion bid to acquire the company.

For now, Game of Thrones remains a key pillar for Warner Bros. Discovery, alongside Harry Potter, Mortal Kombat, and the DC Comics portfolio that includes famous IP like Batman, Superman, and Wonder Woman.

title: New PUBG Game Ded Net Looks Nothing Like PUBG
text:
One of the surprise announcements at Gamescom's Opening Night Live event was PUBG Ded Net, a spin-off with a new premise where "death is only the beginning."

Set in the fictional world of Cascadia in the '90s, Ded Net is a new multiplayer FPS that "combines shooter gameplay with roguelite progression."

That's all there is to go on at this stage, but you can sign up to test the game on Ded Net's website.

It's not surprising to see PUBG expand like this. After all, developer Krafton has said it wants PUBG to become a universe of sorts that spans multiple titles and genres beyond the main battle royale game.

Some of the efforts so far have not worked, as Call of Duty veteran Glen Schofield's horror game The Callisto Protocol was originally envisioned as a PUBG game before dropping its connection to the franchise.

Another spinoff, PUBG Blindspot, shut down after two months.

title: Wait, Is Mega Man: Dual Override Just Mega Man X Now?
text:
Mega Man: Dual Override is delivering another retro-inspired take on the classic Blue Bomber with a release slated next year. But based on his latest trailer revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live, he's cribbing heavily from his sequel series, Mega Man X.

The trailer showed Mega Man using special equipment allowing him to dash, hover, and more. Those moves are familiar for fans of the MMX series, which takes place a hundred years after the original Mega Man. The dashing especially has always set Mega Man X apart, making it a much faster action game. But it appears this new Mega Man title will bring some of that back as well. Mega Man even has some stylized glowy bits on his armor to signify the changes, though it looks more like his robotic paneling is opening up.

It's not clear from the trailer how limited these moves will be, and it's possible they'll be saved for special situations rather than serving as permanent armor upgrades like in the Mega Man X series. And we also saw some other powers that aren't part of the X series, like a rapid-charged fire that absolutely filled the screen with blasts, immediately taking down hapless robot goons.

The trailer also teased a new Robot Master for the series, Twinkle Girl. This will be just the second female robot master, after Mega Man 9's Splash Woman. We haven't yet seen the winner of the design a robot master contest. And just after the announcement, it teased Mega Man and Roll skins coming for Hugh and Diana in Pragmata--which was rumored, before release, to be a stealth Mega Man reboot.

title: Exodus, The New Sci-Fi RPG From Former BioWare Devs, Finally Gets A Launch Date
text:
Archetype Entertainment has just given players another glimpse of its upcoming third-person sci-fi RPG, Exodus, via a new trailer revealed during the Gamescom Opening Night Live ceremony. Even better, the trailer ended with a release date announcement: Exodus is set to launch for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S on April 7.

Exodus' new cinematic gameplay trailer introduces Salt, a companion character who joins the player's party as a skilled mercenary with expertise in long-range sniping. But Salt's most striking feature isn't her prowess in battle—it's the fact that she's a talking octopus who pilots an oversized mech suit.

Salt is an Awakened—a special type of animal that can communicate with humans—and can easily keep up with Exodus' player-character, Jun Aslan, in combat. In the new trailer, Jun and Salt join forces with Emrys (a member of a mysterious hivemind-like species called the Deva) to take on enemies. Emrys can be seen draining power from enemy combatants and transforming it into protection for Jun and Salt, while Salt can be seen deploying inky smokescreens that allow her to reposition herself easily. Together, the trio defeat their attackers, but face a greater enemy: Time. Exodus features Interstellar-style time dilation. A few years in space for Salt is equal to 87 years away from her home planet. In Exodus, players must make decisions that will affect humanity for generations to come.

Exodus is available to wishlist now on the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, Steam, and the Epic Games Store. Archetype Entertainment has implemented wishlist milestones for Exodus, which has already surpassed its first goal of 500,000 wishlist additions, unlocking a Celestial Star Map Decoration for players' in-game apartment, a new batch of concept art, and the first available Exodus music track, "Elegy for a Forgotten World." Other upcoming milestone rewards include cosmetic skins, a Salt-focused story cinematic, and more tracks from the Exodus OST.

title: Genshin Impact Maker’s Nodusfall Sure Looks Like Multiplayer Elden Ring
text:
Gamescom 2026 kicked off with a major surprise in the form of Nodusfall, a multiplayer souls-like from developer Hoyoverse, the studio behind free-to-play gacha games like Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero.

As shown in the trailer and later described by Gamescom Opening Night Live host Geoff Keighley, players take on the roles of Weavers, heroes who must band together to battle "mythic beings" in a world where "divine authority has crumbled and order has collapsed," Keighley said.

The trailer wasn't shy about its inspirations, namely 2022's Elden Ring. Multiple shots in the trailer look like they could have been ripped straight out of From Software's GOTY open-world RPG, including a boss enemy that looks nearly identical to Elden Ring's infamous Malenia. Another boss in the trailer looks extremely reminiscent of Elden Ring's Godfrey, complete with a lion-esque creature.

From Software, of course, released its own multiplayer version of Elden Ring, Elden Ring Nightreign, in 2025. Another multiplayer From Software experiment, The Duskbloods, releases later this year as a Switch 2 exclusive.

Given Hoyoverse's track record, the real question is how Nodusfall will be monetized and if it will feature similar gacha systems to that of the studio's wildly popular open-world action-RPG Genshin Impact.

No release date or platforms for Nodusfall were given, but all of Hoyoverse's previous games have released on PC, with some later coming to consoles as well.

title: Rainbow 6 Tactics Looks Like If Siege And XCOM: Chimera Squad Had A Baby
text:
During Gamescom Opening Night Live, Ubisoft announced the next game in the long-running Tom Clancy series: Rainbow 6 Tactics. The announcement trailer showcased how the turn-based tactics game will play--it looks pretty much like Rainbow Six Siege and XCOM: Chimera Squad had a baby.

And it's entirely single-player, which is great! I love playing Siege, but after years away, I simply cannot enjoy it anymore. The game has too many operators to keep track of (any hero shooter with 50+ characters is too much) and the skill ceiling to enjoy the game is so high--I've simply fallen behind and every month away makes it harder to try and jump back in. Rainbow 6 Tactics looks appealing because it lets me get back into Siege (kinda) without having to worry about other online players.

And the game looks very cool, likely because it's being helmed by Ubisoft Paris, a studio that helped create Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope, which was super excellent for taking the formula for turn-based tactics games and evolving it. In Sparks of Hope's case, it was rewarding the strategy of purposeful movement. Rainbow 6 Tactics seems to also be building on the turn-based-tactics game formula, but instead focusing hard on how a battle starts.

Like Siege, Rainbow 6 Tactics' missions are split into phases. In the initial phase, you use drones to uncover enemy positions, hostage locations, defensive armaments, and more. When that's done, you use whatever information you have to strategize during the breach planning phase, positioning your chosen operators at specific entry points and dictating how they'll get inside--burst through a window, knock down a wall, shoot a target from distance, etc. When you execute, all of your operators then act simultaneously.

From there, the rest of the mission proceeds as most turn-based-tactics games do, with each side taking their turn in combat, trying to land shots depending on a percentage chance to hit, and using cover and special abilities to turn the tide of battle. And you direct one operator at a time, like other games. The one big difference to it seems to take inspiration from Siege: breakable environments. 

And, of course, that first part of every mission looks very different from most other turn-based tactics games. That system of set-up and breach phases really intrigues me. The game seems to be putting a huge onus on trying to set yourself up for success as much as possible on turn one with a perfectly executed and synchronized assault, potentially putting yourself into a tricky scenario if you don't do your due diligence. So many tactics games see you reacting to an enemy already aware of you, so I'm interested to see how a game in the genre works where you essentially have a turn before a mission even begins.

In the game, you play as Paul Bishop, aka Six (a familiar face for those who played Rainbow Six: Vegas 2). You have 15 of Siege's operators under your command and you're trying to rebuild Team Rainbow while still responding to terrorist threats. In a pre-brief for the trailer announcement, we saw Ash, Zofia, Nøkk, Glaz, Doc, Montagne, Sledge, Finka, and Twitch--community developer Emilie Cerkiewicz says that the chosen operators are among the most "iconic" of Siege and that players will see fan-favorites, so I assume the likes of Smoke, Hibana, and Dokkaebi will be there too.

Rainbow 6 Tactics' story will have dozens of handcrafted maps and take place between the events of Siege Year 10 and Year 11 (the current season). This probably means that Year 11 operators Solid Snake and Noor aren't in the game. 

Rainbow 6 Tactics is set to launch in 2027 for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. The game will have no in-game store (like, at all) or in-game monetization systems, and won't be a live-service title--all of which feels impossible for a new Ubisoft game, but that's what Cerkiewicz said during the pre-brief, so who am I to doubt?

title: Humankind 2 Forces You To Deal With The Consequences Of Climate Change
text:
Gamescom Opening Night Live has been dropping trailers for all manner of games, and if you're a fan of historical turn-based strategy games, then you can check out the first look at Humankind 2. Just like the first game, Humankind 2 tasks you with starting a civilization and guiding it through various eras by using diplomacy, military might, and new technologies to stay a step ahead of your rivals. Developer Amplitude Studios says that players can expect the core 4X experience to offer new ways to rewrite history.

According to the developer, Humankind 2 has incorporated feedback from 2021's Humankind to introduce new progression systems, features, enhanced visuals, a modernized user interface, and several other gameplay improvements. Cultural evolution is designed to be deeper, and in each new Era players reach, they can adopt a culture that expands and deepens their civilization's identity. This will, in turn, unlock exclusive customs through expanded cultural progression trees, creating distinct nations throughout the ages.

Of course, players can also stick to the history books when guiding their chosen culture, but new stories from around the world will make it very tempting to experience new scenarios. Amplitude Studios added that the climate will also play a major role, as changing weather systems will transform the strategic map over time. Not only will you need to adapt to climate change, but you'll also need to weigh short-term growth against consequences that may endure for generations.

Humankind 2 will launch for PC in 2027, and if you want to check out the first game, it's on sale for 90% off on Steam until September 8.

title: RollerCoaster Tycoon Is Back, And This Time It Has Bubsy
text:
Atari announced a new RollerCoaster Tycoon title during Gamescom Opening Night Live's pre-show. It's developed by Let's Build a Zoo studio Springloaded and officially titled RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks.

Atari has been the steward for the RollerCoaster Tycoon series since its Infogrames days in the early 2000s, but has not delivered a truly beloved new game in the series in a long time. With Wonderworks, Atari and Springloaded are using Steam Early Access to develop the game alongside the community.

"Early Access offers an opportunity for us to involve this passionate community directly in our development process, helping to sculpt the next great RCT. We want to hear from you! What works? What's missing? What do you want to see in your ideal RCT?" the early access FAQ on the game's Steam page explains. "We have a dedicated roadmap of new parks, rides, and features that we'll roll out throughout Early Access (including water). But in addition, we're leaving space to hear from you and incorporate feedback and suggestions from the community directly into the game."

From the reveal trailer, it seems Wonderworks will play like the classic games in the series, though it sports a new toy-inspired art style for its characters and rides. It also looks like Atari will be taking advantage of all the retro IP it owns for the new game, as we see a Bubsy mascot briefly wandering the park at one point (much to pre-show host Kyle Bosman's chagrin). I guess Bubsy 4D was only the start of the infamous platforming mascot's grand return.

RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks will initially be released as a Steam Early Access game, with Atari planning to keep it in early access for about a year, according to its Steam page. The 1.0 version of the game will feature six parks and a "classic" builder mode that won't be available at the early-access launch.

title: Murals Turns Famous Fairy Tales Into A Silly Action-Adventure
text:
Today, during Gamescom Opening Night Live, Disney Illusion Island developer Dlala Studios introduced its next game: Murals, which puts a new spin on some classic childhood stories, and will launch on PC in 2027.

Murals is an isometric action-adventure game set within multiple famous fairy tales, including Hansel and Gretel, The Little Mermaid, and Rapunzel, but not the way you might remember them. Rapunzel's hair, for example, is actively trying to kill her, while "Sleeping Beauty" is suffering from insomnia and hasn't slept in weeks.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D42nkf8EHMk

Players will control a nameless hero as they fight through these twisted fairy tales with help from Eeries, which the game describes as "mystical, slightly very haunted, doo-dads and whatchamacallits" that enhance the hero's abilities.

Some Eeries enhance the hero's weapon, like Strength In Misery's ability to deal more damage to enemies with status effects, while others affect the hero themselves, like Thorny's passive ability to sometimes damage any attacking enemy that hurts the hero.

Murals, which is developed and published by Dlala, is the studio's first original IP in over a decade. Its most recent projects include Battletoads and 2023's Disney Illusion Island..

title: McDonald’s Halo: Campaign Evolved Skin Has Me Loathin’ It
text:
Eating a Big Mac can help you obtain a special armor set for Master Chief in the UK and Ireland. Thanks to a new McDonald's collaboration with Xbox, there is a new Halo: Campaign Evolved skin that's mainly red and gray, with a yellow visor and flourishes. It costs 1,500 rewards points in the McDonald's app--a tier in the US that will get you a free apple pie, small coffee, or vanilla cone.

Now we could talk about the hilarity of a Master Chief skin for a game predominately played from the first-person perspective, though Halo: Campaign Evolved does let you experience the classic game in third-person. Or we could talk about how this particular armor set (seen below via RebsGaming) looks like something that should be available to just customize within the title's menu. It's really not much more than a palette swap. 

But probably the biggest issue is the armor set, named Side Mission, just screams bland and boring. Like if you're going to have a McDonald's-specific skin in Halo: Campaign Evolved, give it some fun character. Put the iconic "M" arch on Chief's helmet, for instance, sort of like the added decal flair on Magneto's helmet. Or make the visor look like Ronald McDonald, similar to what we did with the horrifying thumbnail on this story.

Now Halo: Campaign Evolved isn't the only Xbox-owned game to get a special reward at McDonald's in the UK and Ireland. The other titles involved in the collaboration are Forza Horizon 6, Fallout 76, Candy Crush Saga, World of Warcraft, and Overwatch. GameSpot has reached out to McDonald's about a similar promotion coming to other parts of the world, including North America.

We also have codes to grab free alternate armor sets in Halo: Campaign Evolved. For more, check out GameSpot's Halo: Campaign Evolved review. The game is available on PC, Xbox Series X|S, and for the first time ever, PS5.
